---
name: comm-create-lazy-claude-codex-skills
description: Use when designing, creating or substantially editing working Codex and Claude skills or rules.
---

# Author one instruction

Use using-superpowers before authoring. Establish task, useful result, intended
harness and destination; cwd is not proof. Before design/substantial edits read
[content and form selection](references/content-contract.md).

1. Inspect existing owners/rules/resources/checks. Covered → reuse; a small gap
   → amend its owner. Select by independent result, not theme or old name.
2. Compare rule-only, lazy-skill-only and rule+skill before choosing. Record why
   each form fits or fails, then select the minimum sufficient form; default
   contextual procedures to lazy skills. A rule needs a concrete pre-selection
   failure that lazy metadata cannot prevent.
3. Produce inputs → actions → result → observable completion, with limits,
   approvals/stops/missing data and exact tested conditions for resource reading.
4. Before writing follow the authorized inbox route from root
   `harness/common/skills/comm-process-harness-inbox/SKILL.md`; keep a full dated
   candidate and permanent rationale/evidence outside working instructions.

Done: justified form and compact complete candidate preserving every contract
and both-mode dependencies. Design alone is not validation or publication.
When checking is requested use
`harness/common/skills/comm-validate-harness-instructions/SKILL.md`;
when publishing use
`harness/common/skills/comm-publish-harness-instructions/SKILL.md`.
Do not load these stages for an unrelated request. Protected entrypoints and
canonical priority remain mandatory.

comm-create-lazy-claude-codex-skills/ref.utf8_text:
# Content and form

Each new/substantial edit: name behavior, trigger and observable result;
inspect existing skills/rules/resources/tests. Covered → reuse without a new
record; a narrow gap → amend its owner. Own request/result/independent check
→ consider a separate owner; one result's detail → conditional resource.
Theme/old name is not ownership; no skill-count quota.

## Select before authoring

Compare all three forms against the actual need:

| Form | Sufficient when |
| --- | --- |
| Rule only | A short boundary must apply before procedure selection; no separate algorithm is needed. |
| Context-dependent lazy skill only | A recognizable task needs a procedure; name/description can trigger its loading. Default for contextual procedures. |
| Rule + lazy skill | A concrete failure must be prevented before skill selection, lazy metadata is insufficient, and the detailed procedure belongs only in matching tasks. |

For a rule, name the pre-selection failure and explain why lazy discovery cannot
prevent it. Brevity, habit and "more reliable" alone are not evidence. A discovery
miss first calls for improving name/description and checking loading; it does
not automatically justify a rule. Preserve existing mandatory boundaries.

Weigh persistent context cost, discovery, procedural cohesion and drift. Choose
the minimum sufficient form, including reuse/no change. Briefly record why each
of the three forms fits or fails, including rejected alternatives, and the choice
in the authorized request or permanent rationale,
outside working instructions. Make technical choices within existing authority;
this adds no universal user approval gate.

In a pair, the rule owns the necessary early boundary and the skill owns the
algorithm. Duplicating a critical boundary needs specific justification; a
mandatory algorithm alone does not justify an always-loaded rule.

When validation is authorized, test form choice and discovery behavior:
lazy-only, rule-only, justified pair, reuse/amendment, metadata repair and
unrelated non-loading. Use real behavior, explicit/implicit discovery and
both-mode checks under the existing validation owner. Missing checks remain
unverified; drafting the rationale is not proof of discovery.

## Preserve the content contract

Write inputs → actions → result → observable completion, when-read pointers,
missing data/approvals/stops/limits. Headings optional; metadata selects.
Remove repeats/advice/history; examples prevent mistakes.
Rationale/evidence permanent outside instructions/inbox. Preserve obligations/
both-mode dependencies with tested pointers, no mandatory chain of all skills.

Goals: SKILL usually ≤200 words; resource sum ≤1000 static tokens,
resolve >1200 deferred; evaluate-skill A/no errors. No raised thresholds,
hidden resources or fake manifests/coverage.

Profile: nonempty YAML name/description; name 1–64 [a-z0-9-], no edge hyphen/--,
folder match, shared comm-/proj-; description 1–1024 chars, trigger/capability.
SKILL alone suffices; references/scripts/assets optional guidance/actions/outputs;
agents/openai.yaml UI/policy/deps. Exclude human bodies.
Rules scope/behavior in body, no paths metadata; Claude ignores metadata
except paths. Verify Codex loading separately.
For new/edited always-loaded rules, before drafting/reporting read from root
`harness/common/skills/comm-validate-harness-instructions/references/rule-budgets.md`.

comm-validate-harness-instructions/SKILL.utf8_text:
---
name: comm-validate-harness-instructions
description: Use when checking an existing harness instruction or candidate, interpreting findings, or establishing its verification status without publication.
---

# Validate the current version

Identify version, target kind, contract, modes, available tools and authorized
checks. Before tests read [validation](references/validation.md); before plugin-eval
read [evaluation](references/evaluation.md). For content/profile checks read from
root `harness/common/skills/comm-create-lazy-claude-codex-skills/references/content-contract.md`.
For new/edited always-loaded rules, before checking/reporting read
[rule budgets](references/rule-budgets.md).

1. Run applicable mandatory checks on the final compact version; separate
   structural, budget, code and native behavior findings. Missing tools/checks
   remain unverified; warn and offer authorized installation.
2. Repair confirmed causes only when authorized, then repeat ALL current
   mandatory checks. Never inflate drafts, thresholds or coverage to get A.
3. Record startup+metadata, comparable actual reads with ALL dependencies and
   full available resources separately, with baseline paths/versions/limits.
4. Report date/version/files/commands/tools/agent versions/scope/contract,
   compactness/actual thresholds/baseline differences/excess reasons,
   pass/fail/not-run/N/A+reason, findings/missing tools/next steps and statuses
   separately for each agent/mode.

Done: truthful current results with no unresolved correctness/discovery/behavior
 gaps for verified scope. Edits reset statuses. This does not publish; copying
or permission never upgrades status. Saving results follows the authorized
inbox/evidence route.

comm-validate-harness-instructions/refer.utf8_text:
# Evaluation

Requires Node + a trusted ordinary installed plugin-eval JS entry in entry.
Do not pass a symlink or resolve a shell shim to bypass rejection; verify the
chosen original entry and ancestors before use. Set skill_dir to selected root:

```sh
node harness/common/scripts/plugin_eval_without_human.mjs "$entry" start "$skill_dir" --format json
```

Then analyze. Own skill folder or bounded generic directory for
plain instructions, not single Markdown. Structural/budget/code findings,
JSON improvementBrief/compare. Save stdout outside target; no --output,
--brief-out/benchmark writes or external metric-packs. README.human.md filter rejects nested/alias reads before content/cost;
sources/tool unchanged. Avoid author-home/cache paths.
Promises API, not OS isolation or protection against concurrent path substitution.
The launcher rejects symlink inputs/ancestors and the whole working harness tree;
interpreter and installed analyzer code remain trusted execution dependencies. After updates rerun via .venv Python pytest:
harness/common/testing/tests/test_plugin_eval_without_human.py.

# Always-loaded rule budgets

Before drafting/checking a new or edited always-loaded rule, measure its complete
UTF-8-decoded text without normalization: `W=len(text.split())`, `C=len(text)`,
`T=(C+3)//4`. Include headings, metadata and line endings. Unicode characters
are not bytes; T is an approximate static estimate, not actual usage/cost.

Report path/version, W, word band, C, T, recommendations and decision:

| Words W | Band |
| --- | --- |
| ≤150 | good |
| 151–300 | moderate |
| 301–500 | heavy-warn |
| >500 | excessive-fail |

For heavy-warn recommend coherent splitting; for excessive-fail strongly recommend
it. Token target: T≤1000; T>1000 warns and recommends remediation; T>1200 strongly
recommends remediation. Evaluate both axes independently; retain analyzer findings
and estimates separately, without changing its thresholds.

For these exceedances present concrete options and await an explicit decision
before dependent work. Permission must cover the current rule/version and relevant
word/token exceptions. Preserve measurements/bands and all other checks; silence,
old approval or permission for publication is not this decision.

Preserve obligations, ownership and form selection when shortening/splitting.
Measure combined reading: splitting always-loaded text alone proves no savings.
Recalculate after edits. Identical native copies represent one rule. This sets no
whole-startup cap and waives no publication gate.

# Checks and behavior

Save contract/scenarios: applicability/actions/completion, limits, permissions,
stops and missing data. RED without new guidance → compact candidate → GREEN;
repeat ALL mandatory checks after edits/before publication. Do not create an
artificial long draft to show shrinkage or artificially shrink compact material.
Applicable skill-creator/external checks are mandatory in every project.

Helpers: using-superpowers; skill-creator design/final quick_validate;
writing-skills behavioral RED–GREEN–REFACTOR; plugin-eval start→analyze;
improve-skill JSON brief→required/recommended fixes→re-evaluate/compare;
openai-docs official sources; plugin-management integration/install.
Evaluate-plugin requires real manifest; plain rules use content/conflicts/
resources/compactness, not skill-only validation. Generic analysis is not
skill/plugin/native proof; installed tool is not verified behavior.
Missing tools → warn, offer authorized install, unverified. Benchmark/config/
dependency writes require authorization; Python dependencies use uv.

Each final version: Codex and Claude separately, common-only neutral project
and combined preserving existing project, native listing, explicit own-resource
invocation, implicit choice, unrelated non-loading and actual behavior.
Check rule reading, loader human exclusion and behavior separately; instructions
do not technically block file access. Installation/template checks read from root
`harness/common/skills/comm-install-harness/SKILL.md`; project-only refuses,
never infer a shared skeleton. For suite/configuration read only as needed
`harness/common/skills/comm-install-harness/references/testing.md`.

Measure baseline/current startup guards+metadata, comparable actual task reads
with complete dependencies, and total available resources separately. Record
paths/versions/factual thresholds/differences/growth/excess reasons/next steps.
Static tokens are not usage/cost; no agreed startup cap. Required resource
remains in its assessed owner; tested when-read pointers and both-mode access.
Report real status/scope; verified needs all mandatory current checks and no
correctness/discovery/behavior gaps. Evidence belongs in testing/evidence,
not checks; retain rationale/results independently of inbox.
